function: Joint learned channel prediction (CNN-LSTM, from past estimated CSI) and outage-constrained multibeam precoding (CNN-FC) at a LEO satellite for weighted sum rate maximization (pp. 1, 4-8).
system: LEO satellite with 16-antenna uniform circular array serving 16 single-antenna IoT devices, 5 GHz (L/S/C band), no RIS (pp. 3, 9).
method: Supervised CNN-LSTM channel predictor (NMSE loss) and unsupervised CNN-FC precoder (penalized quantile outage loss) with VAE channel-error augmentation; offline training with Adam (pp. 4-10).
data_channel: Custom simulated LEO Rician channel (eqs. 1-6, p. 3), parameters set after 3GPP TR 38.821 (p. 9); predictor 16000 train/4000 test samples, precoder 10^6 train/10^3 test (pp. 9-10).
test_conditions: Test samples generated like training samples, each augmented with 10^4 channel errors; sweeps over M, K, fc, d0 do not state reuse of a trained model (pp. 10-12).
baselines: Prediction: linear regression, LSTM, RNN, random forest (Fig. 9). Precoding: MLP, DDPG, BTI (numerical), ZFBF (numerical); non-robust and Gaussian-error variants (Fig. 17) (pp. 10-13).
metrics: NMSE for prediction; weighted sum rate, SINR outage probability, training and validation loss, and execution time for precoding (pp. 9-13).
complexity: Big-O orders of the CNN-LSTM predictor and CNN-FC precoder (p. 9) and measured execution time versus M and K against MLP, DDPG, BTI, ZFBF (Figs. 12-13, p. 11).
openness: none; only states use of open-source TensorFlow 2.11.0 (p. 10), no code or data link.
q1_support: p. 3: "According to the signal propagation characteristics of the LEO satellite communications [25]-[27]" defines a custom Rician channel (eqs. 1-6); p. 9: "set up according to 3GPP TR 38.821" refers to the system parameters of Table I only. No statement that the channel follows TR 38.811 or TR 38.901.
q2_support: p. 10: "103 testing samples which are generated as training samples" (p. 9: "training samples and testing samples are set as 16000 and 4000, respectively"). Sweeps over M, K, fc, d0 and pilot power are not stated to test a model trained elsewhere.
q3_support: p. 11: "MLP scheme proposed in [24], the Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) scheme in [35], the Bernstein-type inequality (BTI) scheme in [36], and the zero-forcing beamforming (ZFBF) scheme"; p. 12: "Fig. 14. The WSR performance comparisons of different schemes under various total transmit powers".
q4_support: p. 9: "we analyze the computational complexity of the two proposed DL-based networks, i.e., DLPDN and DLPCN" (Big-O orders); p. 11: "we adopt the average execution time as the metric to measure the computational complexity performance".
q5_support: p. 10: "The whole model is trained with the open-source machine learning framework Tensorflow 2.11.0" is only a framework; p. 9: "CSI dataset is generated according to (8)" is a custom simulation. No link to code or data, no public dataset.
notes: Area 6: the learned multibeam precoder (weighted sum rate, p. 6) is beam control of a satellite link, more specific than area 3, and the channel prediction (area 2 function) feeds it, so area 6 wins by the tie-break order. For the reviewer: q1 is 0 because TR 38.821 is cited for system parameters (Table I, p. 9), not for the channel model, which is the paper's own Rician model (p. 3). Paper title matches the DOI (Ying et al., LEO satellite IoT).
